records.title: Florida Real Estate Sales Associate: FREC qualification, examination, and activation routes
records.overview: Selected official DBPR and Florida Real Estate Commission (FREC) licensing steps for Florida Real Estate Sales Associates under Florida Statutes Chapter 475 and Florida Administrative Code Rule 61J2. Represents pre-licensing education alternatives (including 63-hour course, real estate degree exemption, Florida Bar attorney exemption, and mutual recognition out-of-state reciprocity), electronic fingerprint screening, Pearson VUE state examination, broker affiliation activation, and mandatory 45-hour post-licensing renewal requirements. This is not a formal legal determination of eligibility; individual applications are evaluated directly by the Department.
records.review_note: Revision 1 establishes the verified FREC sales associate licensing pathway based on F.S. § 475.17, F.A.C. Rule 61J2-3, and DBPR Form RE 1 candidate guidance. Correctly isolates statutory exemptions (active Florida Bar members and four-year real estate degree holders) from the standard 63-hour pre-licensing course, documents non-Florida resident mutual recognition agreements, captures the active-broker registration requirement for valid practice, and highlights the non-extendable 45-hour post-licensing first-renewal condition.

children.label: Complete a FREC-approved 63-classroom-hour pre-licensing Course I for sales associates and pass the course end exam with at least 70%
children.condition: Course completion certificate valid for two years from exam date under Rule 61J2-3.008

children.label: Exempt from pre-licensing education with an accredited four-year degree or higher in real estate
children.condition: Per F.S. § 475.17(2); official university transcripts required with application

children.label: Exempt from pre-licensing education as an active member in good standing of The Florida Bar
children.condition: Per F.S. § 475.17(2); Florida Bar number verified with DBPR; state examination still required

children.label: Qualify under a mutual recognition agreement holding an active real estate license in a recognized qualifying state
children.condition: Non-Florida residents holding active license in AL, AR, CT, GA, IL, KY, MS, NE, RI, or WV; 40-question law exam required

children.label: Be at least 18 years of age and hold a high school diploma or its recognized equivalent
children.condition: F.S. § 475.17(1); United States Social Security number required

children.label: Submit electronic fingerprints through a Florida Department of Law Enforcement (FDLE) approved Livescan service vendor
children.condition: Use DBPR Originating Agency Identifier (ORI) FL920010Z

children.label: Submit completed DBPR RE 1 Application for Real Estate Sales Associate License with required state fees
children.condition: Submit online via DBPR Online Services or by mail; approval required before Pearson VUE testing

children.label: Pass the Florida Real Estate Sales Associate Examination administered by Pearson VUE with a scaled score of 75 or higher
children.condition: 100 multiple-choice questions covering real estate principles, practices, and law

children.label: Mutual recognition candidates: pass the 40-question Florida Real Estate Law examination with a score of 30 or higher (75%)
children.condition: Exempt from general real estate principles section

children.label: Activate license by affiliating with a licensed Florida real estate broker or owner-developer using DBPR Form RE 11
children.condition: Issued in inactive status upon passing exam until registered under an active broker

children.label: Complete a 45-hour FREC-approved post-licensing course prior to the initial license expiration date
children.condition: Mandatory under F.S. § 475.17(3); failure to complete causes license to become null and void without grace period
